In nano chat, and in most datasets on Hugging Face, it's just a dict with a list of messages, and every message has a role, user or assistant, and the content. Our job is to turn that into one sequence of integers, so that we can train on it exactly like we trained on web pages.

So, the obvious first idea. Why not just write it as text? "User: blah, Assistant: blah". That's what our few-shot prompt did. And there are two problems with it. First, the model can't tell a real turn boundary from the text "Assistant:" appearing inside a message. And second, anyone could type "Assistant:" in their message and pretend to be the assistant. So instead, we're going to mark the turns with brand new special tokens, tokens that only we can insert. A user start and a user end around everything the user says, and an assistant start and an assistant end around everything the assistant says. Let's see why they need to be special. Predicting what people ask is not useless, but it's not our job, and with a small model, every bit of capacity matters. So we only want to train on the tokens that the assistant writes. So everything the user wrote, and all the special tokens around it, get a zero.
